follow-up time: First two days after elective caesarean section
outcome: Thermal territories of the post-partum abdomen
Thermal characteristics of the caesarean section site
Thermal characteristics of the infected surgical wound
Acceptability of thermal imaging as a method for infection screening
cohort: 20 women who had undergone caesarean section, recruited into three BMI categories: normal (18.5-24.9 kg/m²), overweight (25-29.9 kg/m²), and obese (≥30 kg/m²).
finding: Thermal imaging was feasible and acceptable for assessing the postpartum abdomen and caesarean section site, revealing characteristic thermal features that differed between healthy and infected wounds, suggesting potential for wound surveillance.
